resources.string: Press the two buttons. Your screenshot is already on the clipboard.
Clipshot needs to see new screenshots to copy them. Choose \"Allow all\": it never reads anything else, and it has no internet access.
Every screenshot goes to the clipboard
Take a screenshot to try it
No internet permission. No account. No tracking.\nNothing ever leaves your phone.
One minute after the copy, the screenshot is deleted from your photos. It stays on the clipboard.
Needs \"All files access\". Clipshot uses it for this one thing.
Take a screenshot from Quick Settings or the accessibility button.
Android only lets apps take a screenshot through an accessibility service. Clipshot\'s service can\'t read your screen; it only presses the screenshot button.
In the accessibility settings, open Clipshot and turn it on.
If Android says the setting is restricted: App info, menu ⋮, Allow restricted settings.
Tap the Capture tile in Quick Settings, or the accessibility button. The screenshot goes to the clipboard.
Screenshot from a tile or the accessibility button

Takes a screenshot when you tap the Capture tile or the accessibility button, so Clipshot can copy it to the clipboard. This service receives no events and can\'t read what is on your screen. Its only action is pressing the screenshot button. Clipshot has no internet access.
